avoid_supplements.name: Echinacea
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May overstimulate immune response and potentially increase risk of splenic rupture or bone pain when combined with filgrastim's myelostimulatory effects
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; counsel patient to discontinue echinacea during filgrastim therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Andrographis paniculata
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent immune stimulant that may potentiate filgrastim's effects and increase adverse events such as bone pain and splenomegaly
avoid_supplements.action: Advise patient to avoid this supplement during treatment course

caution_supplements.name: Astragalus
caution_supplements.mechanism: Immunomodulatory properties may have additive effects with filgrastim; generally considered safe but warrants monitoring
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor for increased bone pain or splenomegaly; discuss with oncology team before use

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild immunostimulatory effects that could theoretically augment filgrastim response
caution_supplements.action: Monitor patient tolerance; no dosage adjustment typically needed but discuss with healthcare provider

caution_foods.name: High-dose vitamin C supplements/foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May theoretically increase oxidative stress in context of rapid myeloid proliferation; generally not contraindicated but warrant moderation
caution_foods.action: Counsel on moderate intake; excessive supplementation should be discussed with oncology team

monitoring_notes: Filgrastim has no significant hepatic metabolism (CYP-independent) and minimal food/supplement interactions; primary concern is avoiding immune-potentiating supplements that may exacerbate myelostimulation-related adverse events like bone pain, splenomegaly, or splenic rupture. Monitor CBC, platelet counts, and clinical symptoms throughout therapy.
